heading: Effective Whole Class Oral Language Interventions and Strategies for Students with Developmental Language Disorder: A Systematic Review
sample: 11 peer-reviewed studies + comparison with 32 web sources
text: The study identifies evidence-based strategies for oral language, vocabulary, grammar and idioms and shows that many recommendations found online have not been studied.
notProven: The whole-class evidence base remains small.
linea: Systematic review with 11 peer-reviewed studies plus comparison with 32 web sources. The whole-class evidence base remains small.

heading: Morphological awareness intervention in children with Developmental Language Disorder: A systematic review
text: The study finds promising evidence for explicit teaching of affixes and word construction.
notProven: Only 4 studies showed significant improvements and there are methodological problems; the evidence remains limited.
linea: Systematic review of 10 studies. Only 4 studies showed significant improvements and there are methodological problems; the evidence remains limited.

heading: Linking Language Skills and Social Competence in Children With Developmental Language Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sample: 15,069 records screened; eligible studies of children aged 2–12
text: The study analyses the association between language skills and social competence in DLD.
notProven: It does not show that social difficulties are caused only by language.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis after screening 15,069 records, with eligible studies of children aged 2–12. It does not show that social difficulties are caused only by language.

heading: The neuroanatomy of developmental language disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study evaluates group-level neuroanatomical differences in DLD.
notProven: It does not produce a clinical diagnostic biomarker and does not allow DLD to be diagnosed using MRI.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. It does not produce a clinical diagnostic biomarker and does not allow DLD to be diagnosed using MRI.

heading: Intervention factors associated with efficacy, when targeting oral language comprehension of children with or at risk for Developmental Language Disorder: a meta-analysis
text: The study examines which components and doses are associated with better comprehension outcomes.
notProven: Observed moderators do not guarantee that any one component is causal.
linea: Meta-analysis. Observed moderators do not guarantee that any one component is causal.

heading: The Use of Language Sample Analysis to Differentiate Developmental Language Disorder From Typical Language in Bilingual Children: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
text: The study evaluates language-sample measures for distinguishing DLD from bilingual language variation.
notProven: Results depend on the languages and measures used; there is no universal rule that applies to every language.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. Results depend on the languages and measures used; there is no universal rule that applies to every language.

heading: Shared characteristics of intervention techniques for oral vocabulary and speech comprehensibility in preschool children with co-occurring features of developmental language disorder and speech sound disorder: a systematic review with narrative synthesis
text: The study looks for common intervention components when vocabulary/language difficulties and speech intelligibility difficulties occur together.
notProven: The evidence on co-occurrence is smaller and not every child responds in the same way.
linea: Systematic review. The evidence on co-occurrence is smaller and not every child responds in the same way.

heading: Effectiveness of physical therapy interventions in children with developmental coordination disorder: a systematic review
text: The study mainly supports task-oriented interventions, with weaker evidence for several supplementary approaches.
notProven: Quality and study designs vary; it does not support any generic exercise programme.
linea: Systematic review of 16 studies. Quality and study designs vary; it does not support any generic exercise programme.

heading: School-based Motor Skill Interventions for Children and Adolescents with Developmental Coordination Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
text: The study found positive effects on motor performance and examined dose/frequency and who delivered the intervention.
notProven: Improving motor performance does not automatically mean improving participation, independence or school outcomes.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 35 studies, 18 in meta-analysis. Improving motor performance does not automatically mean improving participation, independence or school outcomes.

heading: Effect of Coordination Exercises on Hand Function in Patient with Developmental Coordination Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
text: The study found pooled improvement in hand function after coordination exercises.
notProven: Heterogeneity was moderate to high and two studies contributed a large share of the statistical weight.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 7 studies and 361 children. Heterogeneity was moderate to high and two studies contributed a large share of the statistical weight.

heading: Academic Challenges in Developmental Coordination Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
text: The study documents frequent group-level difficulties in handwriting, mathematics and other academic outcomes.
notProven: It does not mean that every child with DCD has academic difficulties or that these are caused exclusively by coordination problems.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 studies. It does not mean that every child with DCD has academic difficulties or that these are caused exclusively by coordination problems.

heading: Motor-Based Interventions in Children with Developmental Coordination Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials
design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
text: The study evaluates effects on motor tests, activity/participation and psychosocial variables.
notProven: Effectiveness varies by intervention type and outcome; not every motor change transfers to everyday life.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials up to January 2024. Effectiveness varies by intervention type and outcome; not every motor change transfers to everyday life.

heading: Criterion A in developmental coordination disorder: Is motor competence efficiently assessed? A systematic review and meta-analysis of mixed evidence from standardized assessments
text: The study examines which motor domains consistently distinguish children and adolescents with DCD from peers.
notProven: Motor batteries are only one part of assessment: diagnosis also requires functional impact and consideration of exclusion criteria and context.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. Motor batteries are only one part of assessment: diagnosis also requires functional impact and consideration of exclusion criteria and context.

heading: Early intervention for children with/at risk of developmental coordination disorder: a scoping review
sample: 103 articles in total; 25 fully or partly related to intervention
text: The study summarises early identification and intervention in children under 5 with or at risk of DCD.
notProven: Formal diagnosis and intervention evidence at very young ages still involve uncertainty.
linea: Scoping review with 103 articles in total and 25 fully or partly related to intervention. Formal diagnosis and intervention evidence at very young ages still involve uncertainty.

heading: Play-integrated augmentative and alternative communication interventions for minimally verbal/nonspeaking children: a systematic review
text: The study reviews AAC interventions integrated into play for autistic children and children with developmental disabilities.
notProven: Samples and participant descriptions are heterogeneous; the review does not support choosing one AAC system for everyone.
linea: Systematic review of 14 studies. Samples and participant descriptions are heterogeneous; the review does not support choosing one AAC system for everyone.

heading: Augmentative and alternative communication interventions with speech-generating devices for autistic preschoolers: a systematic review
text: The study finds moderate to strong effects in some studies and reviews ecological and social validity.
notProven: Fewer than half of the studies met full ecological-validity criteria and only 7 assessed social validity.
linea: Systematic review of 20 studies (1998–2023). Fewer than half met full ecological-validity criteria and only 7 assessed social validity.

heading: A systematic review of interventions for echolalia in autistic children
text: Most interventions attempted to reduce echolalia, but overall study quality was very low and its communicative function was often ignored.
notProven: It does not justify a general clinical recommendation to 'eliminate' echolalia.
linea: Systematic review of 15 studies. It does not justify a general clinical recommendation to 'eliminate' echolalia.

heading: Intervention techniques targeting echolalia in autistic people: a scoping review
text: The study confirms that much of the literature focuses on reduction and that few studies measure functional communication.
notProven: Mapping studies is not the same as demonstrating effectiveness; it reinforces caution about purely reduction-focused goals.
linea: Scoping review of 74 articles. Mapping studies is not the same as demonstrating effectiveness; it reinforces caution about purely reduction-focused goals.

heading: Auditory Processing Disorder in Childhood: A Critical Review
text: The study highlights overlap with DLD, dyslexia, ADHD and autism and questions the validity of some diagnostic tools during development.
notProven: APD should not be used as an automatic explanation for every difficulty hearing in noise.
linea: Critical review. APD should not be used as an automatic explanation for every difficulty hearing in noise.

heading: Misophonia: a systematic review of current and future trends in this emerging clinical field
text: The study describes an emerging field with wide variation in definitions and assessment tools.
notProven: It does not validate one universal diagnosis and does not support equating misophonia with hyperacusis or APD.
linea: Systematic review. It does not validate one universal diagnosis and does not support equating misophonia with hyperacusis or APD.
